subject: Post-demo: Redwood Inference — buying committee recap & procurement path
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@averysystems.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-10T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: Redwood Inference — buying committee recap & procurement path

Jordan — thanks again for the time today. Quick written recap of what we covered in the demo plus the proposed next steps so your committee has a single place to reference.

1) Demo highlights (quick bullets)
- Multi-mode deployment demonstrated: Hosted API + Dedicated pool and private VPC option.
- Live latency profiling: sub-120ms p95 on the sample prompt set with the recommended batching profile.
- Cost levers: quantization profile, autoscale burst vs committed throughput, and prefix caching.
- Observability: token-level cost and per-route latency dashboards + regression alerts.

2) Stakeholder map (as we heard today)
- Economic buyer: Jordan Lee (CPO) — owns budget and final approval.
- Procurement lead: Samir Patel — contract/payment terms, PO process.
- Security reviewer: Laura Chen — SOC2, data residency, SSO/SCIM.
- Technical reviewer / implementer: Marta Diaz (engineering) — integration, rollout plan.
- Product (UX) stakeholder: Ben Carter — acceptance criteria for quality/regression.

3) Decision criteria we logged in-session
- Compliance: SOC2 + audit logs and optional VPC/on-prem for regulated workloads.
- Performance: p95 latency target <=150ms for the 512-token profile.
- Cost: predictable unit economics for 1M token volumes; ability to reserve capacity.
- Ops: ability to pin model versions, A/B rollouts, and tracing hooks for debugging.

4) Immediate asks / gaps
- Procurement form / billing contact (Samir) — needed to start SOW/PO flow.
- Security questionnaire & evidence — Laura requested SOC2 report and sample retention policy.
- Pilot scope & metrics — suggested 60-day pilot with 3 KPI checks (latency, cost per 100k tokens, error rate).

5) Proposed next steps (concrete owner / ETA)
- I (Connor) will share the Redwood security overview (SOC2 + artifact list) and a one-page pilot plan by EOD tomorrow. (Owner: Connor)
- Samir to confirm procurement contact and provide any internal PO template or procurement form. (Owner: Samir; ETA: ~1 week)
- Rishi to schedule a 30-min call with Marta to walk through integration specifics and SSO/SCIM. (Owner: Rishi; ETA: 48–72 hrs)
- Marissa to prepare two pricing options (pilot + committed rate) and a draft commercial term summary. (Owner: Marissa; ETA: 2 business days)

If the stakeholder mapping above is off, tell me and I will adjust. If you can loop in Samir and Laura on the same thread (or share their preferred contact) we can kick procurement/security in parallel to technical onboarding.

Attachments we will share right after this email: Redwood_Security_Overview_v2.pdf (SOC2 + retention + SSO notes) and a sample pilot statement of work.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this toward a pilot.

—
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@averysystems.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Redwood Inference — buying committee recap & procurement path

Thanks Connor — that summary is great and matches what I heard internally. A few quick notes:

- Procurement: looping Samir on this thread (cc'd). He has an internal procurement form and prefers we return a filled copy — Samir, I think the easiest path is for you to send the template and we'll populate it.
- Security: Laura, can you confirm whether a SOC2 report + the retention policy doc will be sufficient to begin the security review? If you need additional artifacts (e.g., pen test results) let us know.
- Timeline: our goal is to complete procurement/legal review within 1–2 weeks, then technical review in parallel. Final budget sign-off expected in ~2 weeks from now assuming no major redlines.

Decision pivot we discussed: our leadership is leaning toward the Dedicated deployment if Redwood can guarantee predictable p95 at scale and provide a clear pilot exit criteria.

Jordan

Jordan / team — appreciate the quick turnaround on timeline. A few operational items from our side to accelerate:

- Pricing / commercials: I'm putting together two commercial options: (A) 60-day pilot (hosted) with option to convert to Dedicated with a 12-month reserved commit; (B) Immediate Dedicated pilot with a reduced pilot rate and a short-term reserve. I will attach a one-page summary.
- Security artifacts: Connor will share the standard security pack. If Laura needs anything beyond that (pen test, encryption at rest detail), we can get legal to share those artifacts under an NDA.
- Procurement: Rishi — can you please book a 30-min intro between Samir and our procurement lead (Markus Klein) to run through payment terms and PO flow? Markus is cc'd on my internal calendar invite (will share separately).

Proposed immediate next meeting: 30 minutes next Thursday (May 14) to bring procurement + security + engineering on the call and align pilot acceptance criteria. If that works for you Jordan, we'll send a meeting invite with an agenda.

Note on acceptance criteria — here's what we'll propose in the pilot SOW:
- Stabilized latency: p95 under 150ms for the agreed prompt set.
- Request success rate > 99.5%
- Cost within x% of projected run-rate (we'll define exact thresholds in the SOW).

Connor / Rishi: please use this thread to drop the security overview and the sample SOW.

Best,
Marissa Cole
